slots.label: Preferred language
slots.instruction: The language the learner writes in: en, he, or mixed. Judged from the script of their prompts, never from their location.
slots.impacts: Reply language and which text versions to show first.

slots.label: Hebrew reading level
slots.instruction: How well the learner reads Hebrew. Evidence: writing Hebrew in prompts, asking for translations of Hebrew, asking what a Hebrew word means. Keep this separate from comfort with study terms: someone can read Hebrew and still not know what a sugya is.
slots.impacts: Whether to offer Hebrew with translation, transliteration, or English only.

slots.label: Comfort with study terms
slots.instruction: How comfortable the learner is with Jewish study vocabulary (sugya, gemara, remez, halakhah). Evidence: using such terms without explanation, or asking what they mean. Separate from Hebrew reading ability.
slots.impacts: Whether terms are defined inline and how dense the answer is.

slots.label: Preferred register
slots.instruction: Whether the learner studies inside the tradition (how the commentators read a source) or in the academic register (dating, context, textual criticism). Set only by code or a typed yes/no or one-of-N answer, never by free-text model consolidation.
slots.impacts: Whether answers lead with the classical commentators or with historical and critical context.

slots.label: Texts they study
slots.instruction: Up to three corpora the learner keeps returning to. Evidence: the books and corpora they ask about or cite. Only recurring interests, not a single question.
slots.impacts: Which links and follow-up directions to offer.

slots.label: Preferred answer style
slots.instruction: How the learner wants answers shaped (length, depth, format, tone), written in the second person and describing the answer, never the person. Example: 'Keep answers short and lead with the source.'
slots.impacts: Length, structure and tone of the reply.

slots.label: Learning habits
slots.instruction: A study cycle or position the learner is following, in the second person (for example the daf or parashah they are on). Only from repeated evidence across sessions.
slots.impacts: Suggesting the next step in their cycle.
